# Hutch

> Hutch is a local-first, MIT-licensed platform for personal AI assistants that run on your own Linux computer. You choose the models and connected apps; assistants ask for your approval before important actions. The source is public and MIT-licensed on GitHub; there are no packaged desktop installers.

Hutch keeps its control state — conversations, memory, logs, schedules and files — in one local state directory on the machine you control. Model calls go to the route you confirm for each assistant: a local runtime (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio) or a hosted provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, or OpenCode). On first run Hutch may preselect a free OpenCode model as a disclosed starting point; free hosted models can keep or learn from what you send, and nothing is saved until you create the assistant. Hosted providers receive the prompts and context Hutch sends them; network tools contact their own destinations.

Local and offline are scoped claims. In Strict Offline, the run's worker has no network namespace and its only model path is a per-run Unix socket fixed to the reviewed loopback origin, so Hutch may say that this run's worker could not reach the network and its model route went only to loopback. A separately running Ollama, llama.cpp or LM Studio process is outside that boundary: it may check for updates, pull a model or forward a cloud-tagged request, and loopback addressing does not prove it stays local. The owner-approved Hutch-managed isolated model process (ADR-0035) is not implemented. Hutch does not claim that nothing left the machine.

## Key facts

- Site: https://k-arthur.github.io/hutch/ (single static page, GitHub Pages).
- Status: development preview. The MIT-licensed source is public on GitHub; there are no packaged desktop installers and no hosted sign-up.
- Platform: Linux (Python 3.11+). macOS and Windows executors are not implemented.
- License: MIT. The software is free; hosted model usage is billed by your own provider account.
- Assistants (called bots in the CLI): each has its own model, tools, schedule, memory and workspace.
- Approvals: assistants ask before consequential actions; some shell command classes are always denied; there is no bulk approval.
- Local runtimes: Ollama, llama.cpp and LM Studio are first-class routes on 2026-11-06 evidence (Ollama 0.40.13/0.40.15, llama.cpp b12144, LM Studio llmster 0.0.27-1). Hutch reads their reported version, loaded models, applied window and vision/tool support and labels a model that leaves the machine. The evidence is one Linux host; GPU, vLLM, SGLang, macOS and Windows were not verified.
- Data-sharing confirmation: switching an existing assistant to a cloud-tagged or non-loopback model requires a recorded per-assistant confirmation; the save or one-message use consumes it once, and switching back asks again.
- Spend controls: estimated budgets, usage reservations and per-bot ceilings; provider billing stays authoritative.
- Chat input: text plus PNG/JPEG/WebP image attachments (up to 4 per message, 1.5 MB each); built-in runtimes need a vision-capable model route, and the OpenCode runtime checks the selected model's declared image support.
- Schedules: IANA-timezone recurring tasks that catch up after sleep while the local service is running; nothing runs while the machine is off.
- Personal operations: durable commitments with due dates, provenance and completion evidence; a deterministic Today view of approvals, commitments, scheduled work and real run state; shared household/project spaces with explicit, revocable per-assistant access. Assistants may propose commitments and report completion, but only the owner confirms or verifies them. The local server remains single-owner: spaces scope data and record members, they are not separate logins.
- Deletion: a governed two-step permanent deletion for one whole assistant (`hutch bot destroy`, the typed deletion API or the dashboard danger zone), with content-free evidence; backups, exports, provider-side copies and folder-mode workdirs are not erased.
- Evidence: what works, what is experimental and what is unavailable is documented in the repository (docs/realignment/baseline.md and docs/marketing-site.md).

## Not claims

- No public install command, package or download exists today; the supported path is a Linux source checkout. Unsigned Ubuntu deb/AppImage builds exist only as local acceptance output and are not published.
- Hutch does not operate models itself; it connects to model routes you configure.
- Usage estimates are not provider-enforced spending limits.

- Repository: https://github.com/K-Arthur/hutch — the README and the repository's evidence ledger are the canonical summary of current capabilities.
